transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you here — what would you like to talk about or get help with?

I… I came because after some nights when I’ve been eating, I end up sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I just feel so ashamed. Disgusted with myself, really. The next morning I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, exercising a lot, or using laxatives?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I don’t think I do those things, not in any planned way. I mostly just feel bad afterward and try not to think about it.
During these times when you're eating, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yes… I do. Once I’ve had that first bite, especially when the house is quiet, it’s like I can’t quite make myself stop. I’ll be thinking, Belinda, that’s enough now, but my hands just keep going back for more.
Do these episodes of eating happen more when you're feeling stressed, sad, or upset about something?
I’m not really sure. I mean… sometimes I’m upset, I suppose, but I haven’t really paid close attention to whether that’s when it happens more.
Have these eating episodes caused you a lot of distress or gotten in the way of your daily life, like work, relationships, or other activities?
A little, yes… I’ve started saying no to some bridge nights and helping in the church kitchen. I just get worried someone will notice things missing, or ask why I’m acting so… ashamed, I suppose.
How often do these eating episodes happen — do they occur at least once a week, or are they less frequent?
It’s… at least once a week. Usually once or twice most weeks, I’d say. Since my friend passed, it hasn’t really gone a whole month where it eased up.
When you're having one of these eating episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control, like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Yes… I suppose so. Once I take that first bite, especially when the house is quiet, it’s like my better judgment just… steps aside. I’ll tell myself, “Belinda, stop now,” but my hands keep reaching for more anyway.
When these eating episodes happen, do they have a clear beginning and end — like you start eating and then eventually stop, rather than just grazing or snacking continuously throughout the day?

Yes… it’s more like it starts, and then it ends when I’ve… eaten too much. On a bad night I might begin with leftovers, like casserole, and then it turns into brownies, biscuits, chicken salad… all in one sitting. It’s not really all-day nibbling.
Do you feel a lot of distress or concern about your body shape or weight, especially in relation to these eating episodes?
I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I don’t like thinking about it much. I suppose I do feel upset afterward, but… about my shape or weight specifically, I don’t know. I try not to look too closely.
Have these eating episodes caused any problems with your friends, family, or within your community, beyond what you've already mentioned?
A little, yes. I’ve… started saying no to bridge nights sometimes, and to helping in the church kitchen. I worry someone will notice leftovers gone, or ask why I’m acting so ashamed.
Do these eating episodes happen even when you’re not really hungry, like when you’re already full but still feel compelled to keep eating?
Yes… even when I’m not hungry. I keep going until my stomach feels tight and sore, and then I have to sort of ease myself into the recliner because moving hurts.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or daily functioning, like feeling down or having trouble concentrating, after these eating episodes?
Yes… I feel awful after. I just sit there with the crumbs and empty containers, and I’m so ashamed with myself. Next morning it’s hard to pray, or even look people at church in the eye.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you’re embarrassed about how much you’re eating?
Yes… I do. At bridge or church suppers I’ll take just a small plate, so it looks normal. Then later, when everyone’s gone, I’ll go back in the kitchen and eat the leftovers where nobody can see me.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of these eating episodes?
I… I don’t know. I have my quiet days, I suppose, but I’m not sure it’s like that outside of what happens after I eat.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of these eating episodes?
I’m not really sure. I still do some things… I just don’t always feel much like myself, I guess. It’s hard to separate it all.
Have you had days when you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even when you weren’t dealing with these eating episodes?
I’m… not sure I can say. Some days I’m just quieter, but I haven’t really noticed if it’s separate from all that.
Have you had several days in a row where you felt down or didn’t take pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even when you weren’t thinking about eating episodes?
I don’t really know. I haven’t kept track of it like that… sometimes I’m low for a bit, but whether it’s several days and not about the eating, I’m not sure.
Have you had a period where you felt down nearly every day or lost interest in things you usually care about for two weeks or more, even when it wasn’t related to these eating episodes?
I don’t know… two weeks sounds pretty specific. I can’t really say it’s been like that nearly every day, or separate from the eating stuff. I just haven’t kept track.
Have you had a time when you felt down or didn’t care about things you usually enjoy for two weeks or more, even when it wasn’t connected to the eating episodes?
I’m sorry, I really don’t know. I can’t say there’s been a clear two-week stretch like that. I just… haven’t paid attention to it that way.
